summary: The bill amends the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to bar the Secretary of Energy from issuing any new or revised energy conservation standards for appliances or other products unless they are technologically feasible, economically justified without increasing net consumer costs, and deliver significant energy or water savings, while also prohibiting new standards for distribution transformers.

The bill substantially revises Section 325 of the Energy Policy and Conservation Act to impose stricter requirements (technological feasibility, economic justification without net consumer costs, minimum energy savings thresholds, disclosure of foreign ties, etc.) before new or amended efficiency standards can be issued. It also freezes new standards for distribution transformers and limits the scope of standards for certain appliances. These changes make it materially harder to adopt energy- and water-efficiency rules that reduce consumption and emissions, thereby limiting environmental regulation.
